title: The Inner Planets
summary: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are the four rocky planets closest to the Sun. They are small and dense, with solid surfaces and few or no moons.

glossary.definition: A planet made mostly of rock and metal, with a solid surface. Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are the Solar System's terrestrial planets.
glossary.analogy: Like a stone you can stand on, compared with a gas giant, which is more like a cloud with no floor.
glossary.example: A spacecraft can land on Mars because it is a terrestrial planet.

glossary.definition: The curved path an object takes around a star, planet or moon, held in place by gravity.
glossary.analogy: Like a ball on a string swung around your head: the string is gravity.
glossary.example: Earth completes one orbit of the Sun in about 365.25 days.

glossary.definition: The warming of a planet's surface when its atmosphere traps heat from sunlight.
glossary.example: Venus's thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere makes it hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

flashcards.front: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
flashcards.explanation: Mercury is also the smallest planet. It has almost no atmosphere, so it can't hold on to heat at night.

flashcards.front: What is the hottest planet in the Solar System?
flashcards.explanation: The Greenhouse Effect from its thick atmosphere keeps Venus at around 465 °C, hotter than Mercury.

flashcards.back: Iron oxide (rust) in its soil and dust.

flashcards.front: How long does one Orbit of the Sun take for Earth?
flashcards.explanation: The extra quarter day is why a leap day is added every four years.

quiz.question: Which of these is a Terrestrial Planet?
quiz.explanation: Mars is rocky with a solid surface. The other three are giant planets made mostly of gas or ice.

quiz.question: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury?
options: It is closer to the Sun
It has active volcanoes on every continent
quiz.explanation: Mercury is closer to the Sun, but Venus's dense carbon-dioxide atmosphere causes a runaway greenhouse effect.
